title: Viomycin as a Wikidata therapy-edge leftover
dek: P2176 on Q12204 still lists this historic peptide. It is not Group A. Capreomycin is the better-known cousin already plated.
story: Viomycin appears on Wikidata as a drug-or-therapy edge for tuberculosis and has an English Wikipedia page as a tuberactinomycin peptide antibiotic. That is graph fuel: the encyclopedia remembers drugs programmes have largely left.
Capreomycin is the cousin Simplfy already treats as a named second-line injectable with ototoxicity/renal baggage. Do not resurrect viomycin because SPARQL returned it.
The pedagogical win is to treat P2176 as a lagging historic list — same lesson as missing bedaquiline on that edge.
deepTitle: Why keep a 'do not use this as a backbone' card
deep: Peptide anti-TB drugs share ribosomal themes with capreomycin/amikacin stories; they are not interchangeable without DST.
WHO Group C injectables are a clinic ranking, not a SPARQL ranking.
If a genome pipeline annotates a 'viomycin resistance gene' from an old database, translate to the drugs you actually report.
